title: Vrata client compatibility
assumptions: Statuses describe the named client profile with the relevant Vrata feature enabled on a correctly configured HTTPS self-host.
Chromium mobile emulation and synthetic WebXR validate fallback behavior only; they do not qualify a physical mobile or headset profile as supported.
A capability remains untested until qualifying evidence exists for the exact profile.

statusDefinitions.supported: The measurable capability scenario passed on the exact profile and revision without a known blocking defect.
statusDefinitions.degraded: The primary scenario passed, but a verified limitation affects expected behavior and is documented below.
statusDefinitions.unsupported: The scenario reproducibly failed on the exact profile or is excluded by a documented platform decision.
statusDefinitions.untested: No qualifying evidence exists for the exact profile.

capabilities.label: Join
capabilities.passCriteria: The client completes access and room join, then appears in presence without a crash.

capabilities.label: Movement
capabilities.passCriteria: Local input changes pose and another client receives the current position without a stale participant.

capabilities.label: Voice
capabilities.passCriteria: The client publishes and receives LiveKit audio, and mute state remains synchronized.

capabilities.label: Spatial audio
capabilities.passCriteria: Remote audio follows participant pose or uses an explicitly documented degraded fallback.

capabilities.label: Screen share
capabilities.passCriteria: The client publishes a display track, another participant sees the in-room surface, and stop clears the state.

capabilities.label: Presentation
capabilities.passCriteria: An authorized presenter opens content and changes presentation state that an observer can see.

capabilities.label: WebXR
capabilities.passCriteria: The client enters immersive VR, publishes XR pose, and exits without disconnecting room or audio.

profiles.label: Desktop Chromium on Linux CI
profiles.notes: Results apply to the recorded Linux CI/staging profile and do not automatically cover Windows or macOS.

profiles.label: Android Chrome
profiles.notes: Chromium touch emulation is covered by CI, but no current physical Android run is recorded.

profiles.label: iOS Safari
profiles.notes: Safari user-agent emulation in Chromium is not evidence for a physical Apple device.

profiles.label: Meta Quest Browser
profiles.notes: Historical headset checks exist, but their exact current device and browser versions were not recorded, so they do not qualify this profile.

evidence.label: CI Chromium room and cross-device scenarios
evidence.notes: The runtime and cross-device Playwright shards passed with the bundled Chromium browser. Mobile emulation in the same run is not used as physical-device evidence.

evidence.label: Staging voice and spatial-audio gate
evidence.notes: The public HTTPS staging gate validated LiveKit media and spatial source attachment on the deployed revision.

knownIssues.summary: Historical Quest checks reported improved but not perfectly smooth remote motion; the current headset/browser profile has not been revalidated.
knownIssues.workaround: No known workaround. Keep the capability untested until a fresh headset run records exact versions and current behavior.
